problems: Caption says Truffle 'walks in' during the close shot, but the pig walks in only in the wide shot (storyboard frames 6-8). From the first close frame (frame 9) to the last (frame 16), the pig is already standing there and its legs never move, so the close shot shows a frozen pose, not an arrival.

Caption says it 'stands right on' the biscuit, but it does not clearly do that. In the 50% frame the trotter stands on the grass beside the biscuit. In the 75% frame and frames 10-16 it only overlaps the rim. In frame 9 the hoof sinks into the biscuit and goes through it.

Nothing reacts to the contact. The biscuit does not tilt, crack or press down under a pig's weight. The ants around it keep the same ring and the same trail while a huge hoof stands next to them (frames 9-16, 50% and 75% frames).

The pig's front legs have broken jagged seams: red-brown torn zigzag lines across the leg near the belly in the 50% and 75% frames and in all of storyboard frames 9-16. In frame 9 the torn edge looks like a loose flap.

In the wide shot (25% frame, frames 1-8), the ants are scattered specks, and the orange arc and the black line next to it are hard to tell apart. Someone new cannot tell which one is the 'honey road' or that the orange disc is a biscuit. Falling leaves and the leaf shadows across the ground add even more clutter.
The close shot is framed so low that the pig's belly fills the top half and the pig cannot be recognised as Truffle. A viewer only sees pink legs.
posts.critique: The caption describes an action in the close shot that the film never shows: the pig is already in place, frozen, and its hoof only touches the biscuit's edge, and neither the biscuit nor the ants react. The torn seams on the pig's legs are clearly visible right at the centre of the shot.
